answer: We formalize a consensus mechanism where stakers in a decentralized grove commit dynamic opportunity-cost bonds tied to zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs. Should an adversary project Sybil identities across a network knoll or route attacks via a comet node, the subgame-perfect slashing matrix executes deterministic collateral forfeitures. Because capital constraints scale superlinearly against identity multiplication, expected attack utility is strictly negative, forcing adversarial multi-agent systems to converge to a strict Nash equilibrium.
